extracted.intended_audience: shippers, carriers, package designers/manufacturers, and regulatory compliance officers for radioactive material transportation (DOT/NRC licensees)
extracted.subtask_description: Federal final rule amending the Hazardous Materials Regulations to harmonize with IAEA TS-R-1: adopts new indices and labels, revises packaging, marking, segregation, and air-transport controls, phases out older DOT specification packagings, and sets transition and preemption rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit CSI for passenger aircraft
rubrics_metrics.description: Limit the Criticality Safety Index (CSI) to a maximum of 3.0 for a fissile material package transported in a passenger carrying aircraft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Necessary because the historical 3.0 TI limit on passenger aircraft would only limit radiation hazard and not the criticality hazard; explicitly replaces prior reliance on TI for criticality concerns in passenger aircraft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive use for high-CSI air shipments
rubrics_metrics.description: Any package, overpack or consignment having a criticality safety index greater than 50 shipped by air must be transported under exclusive use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New paragraph (e) added to ensure CSI > 50 air shipments are exclusive use to control criticality hazard during air transport.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate cargo aircraft TI/CSI limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Include requirements for cargo aircraft only based on separate TS-R-1 limits on total Transport Index (TI) and total Criticality Safety Index (CSI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 175.702(b) revised to reflect cargo-aircraft-specific cumulative TI and CSI limits; differentiates cargo vs passenger aircraft controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special arrangements for high radiation packages by air
rubrics_metrics.description: Packages with radiation levels higher than those allowed by the regulations may be transported by air under special arrangements approved by the Associate Administrator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §175.703(c) revised to allow higher-than-normal radiation packages by air only if special arrangements are approved — approval authority is the Associate Administrator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of groups containing fissile material
rubrics_metrics.description: Groups of radioactive material packages containing fissile material must be separated by at least 6 m (20 feet) from all other such groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirement moved into §176.704 from §176.700; separation distance used to manage criticality/shipping segregation on vessels/transport.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt Criticality Safety Index (CSI) distinct from Transport Index (TI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt the CSI to refer to what was formerly the criticality control transport index, and restrict the concept of Transport Index to a number derived purely from the maximum radiation level at one meter from the package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §176.704 revision and Description of Actions clarify decoupling of TI (radiation at 1 m) and CSI (criticality control), and replacement of Table III with Table IIIA (Transport Index Limits) and Table IIIB (Criticality Safety Index Limits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate method for segregation distances — limited use
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide detailed dose rate guidance for an alternate method to determine segregation distances, restricted to the case of exclusive use shipments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternate method per latest IMDG Code; use of alternate method limited to exclusive use shipments for which §176.704(f) requires a radiation protection program approved by the competent authority of the flag state of the vessel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replace TI references with CSI for fissile packages
rubrics_metrics.description: Replace references to transport index for fissile material packages with references to criticality safety index.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §177.842 revisions reflect the metric shift to CSI as the operative control variable for fissile material packages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Package marking requirements and removal of redundant wording
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove the wording 'and Radioactive Material' from the marking requirement (duplicative), require each package to comply with marking requirement of §178.3(a)(2), and require each DOT specification packaging to be marked with the name and address or symbol of the manufacturer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §178.350(b) revised and new §178.350(c) added; clarifies marking obligations including manufacturer identification on DOT specification packagings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase out specific DOT specification packagings
rubrics_metrics.description: Discontinue authorization for DOT Specification 6L and 6M metal packagings as fissile material packaging, and DOT Specification 20WC and 21WC protective jackets/overpacks as Type B packagings — removing §§178.352, 178.354, 178.362, 178.364 in their entirety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because these 1967-based designs have not been shown to meet later IAEA standards, the rule removes their authorization; transitional provisions (see transition entries) apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt nuclide-specific exemption activity concentrations and consignment activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt the nuclide-specific exemption activity concentrations and the nuclide-specific exemption consignment activities listed in TS-R-1 to maintain consistency between domestic and international regulations for the basic definition of radioactive material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of harmonization with TS-R-1; also provides an exception for certain naturally occurring radioactive materials not exceeding 10 times exemption values (see related criterion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception for certain naturally occurring radioactive materials (NORM)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an exception in the HMR that certain naturally occurring radioactive materials would not be subject to the HMR so long as their specific activities do not exceed 10 times the activity concentration exemption values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This limits regulatory scope for low-activity NORM consistent with TS-R-1 adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporate TS-R-1 A1 and A2 value changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate the TS-R-1 changes in the A1 and A2 values into the HMR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A1/A2 values determine activity thresholds for different packaging and shipment classifications; updating to TS-R-1 aligns domestic thresholds with international practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt new proper shipping names and UN identification numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt the new proper shipping names and UN identification numbers from TS-R-1, except for those referring to Type C packages, fissile LSA material, and fissile SCOs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Updates shipping descriptions to match international nomenclature while excluding certain Type C/fissile categories pending other decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: SI units requirement with customary units in parentheses
rubrics_metrics.description: Require, if customary units are used, that the appropriate quantity and customary units be placed within parentheses positioned after the original quantity expressed in the International System of Units (SI units).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures SI-first presentation with customary units optional and parenthetical for clarity and international consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fissile label and CSI notation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Require the new fissile label be placed on each fissile material package, and that the CSI for that package be noted on the fissile label.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New labeling requirement to communicate criticality safety information directly on package; improves hazard communication to shippers, carriers, and emergency responders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excepted and industrial packaging marking requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Excepted packages must be marked with the UN identification number; industrial packagings must be marked with the package type; Type IP-2 and IP-3 industrial packages and Type A packages must be marked with the international vehicle registration code of the country of origin of packaging design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standardizes markings to convey packaging class and origin; intended to remove redundant markings and improve clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove redundant 'Radioactive Material' shipping-description requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove requirement that the shipping description contain the words 'Radioactive Material' where those words are already included in the proper shipping name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eliminates redundancy after adoption of new proper shipping names that already include the class wording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove Pu-238 from fissile material definition and lists
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove plutonium-238 (Pu-238) from the definition of fissile material and remove the reference to Pu-238 in the list of fissile radionuclides for which weight may be listed instead of or in addition to activity in shipping papers or label descriptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alters the scope of fissile definitions and associated documentation requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt definition of contamination and authorities for unpackaged LSA/SCO and qualified containers
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt a definition of contamination, include an authority to transport unpackaged LSA material and SCO, and an authority to use qualified tank containers, freight containers and metal intermediate bulk containers as industrial packagings, types 2 and 3 (IP-2 and IP-3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies what constitutes contamination and expands permitted container types for certain LSA/SCO materials under defined conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt new LSA-I material class
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt the new class of LSA-I material, consisting of radioactive material in which the activity is distributed throughout and the estimated average specific activity does not exceed 30 times the activity concentration exemption level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replaces older category referencing mill tailings/contaminated earth/etc.; sets numeric upper bound for LSA-I classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: UF6 packaging and certification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate TS-R-1 changes for packagings containing more than 0.1 kg of uranium hexafluoride (UF6); require UF6 packagings to meet the pressure, drop and thermal test requirements, prohibit the use of pressure relief devices, and certify the packagings in accordance with TS-R-1 requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies performance tests and the prohibition of pressure relief devices for UF6 packagings; certification must follow TS-R-1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base fissile shipment non-exclusive/exclusive use on CSI limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Revise §§173.453, 173.457 and 173.459 to remove references to 'fissile material, controlled shipment' and to base requirements for non-exclusive use and exclusive use shipments of fissile material packages on TS-R-1 package and conveyance CSI limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shifts decision criteria for exclusive vs non-exclusive shipments to package/conveyance CSI thresholds from previous 'controlled shipment' constructs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit manufacture of 1967 Type B specification packages
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibit the manufacture of all Type B specification packages conforming to Safety Series No. 6 (1967) as of the effective date of this rule, while allowing continued use of these packages for a limited transition period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New manufacture banned immediately on effective date; continued use allowed for a transition (see transition-period entries); rationale: 1967 designs lack later safety enhancements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement that active material be enclosed in excepted packages
rubrics_metrics.description: Add a requirement that the active material in an instrument or article intended to be transported in an excepted package be completely enclosed by the non-active components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures that active radioactive components in instruments/articles shipped as excepted packages are not exposed; reduces contamination/leak risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition period for phasing out 1967 packagings
rubrics_metrics.description: Permit continued use of currently authorized DOT specification 6L, 6M, 20WC, and 21WC packagings for a period of 4 years after the effective date of the final rule (effective date Oct 1, 2004; industry will have a 5-year period from publication).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extended transition (relative to NPRM) to give industry time to requalify or replace packagings; the rule estimates industry costs and stages phase-out accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: No new reporting or recordkeeping requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: This final rule includes no new reporting or recordkeeping requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paperwork Reduction Act entry confirms existing OMB-approved collection remains applicable; provides OMB approval details (No. 2137-0510).

rubrics_metrics.name: DOT and NRC regulatory roles and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: DOT regulates both shippers and carriers (packaging requirements; shipping-paper contents; package labeling/marking; vehicle placarding; training and emergency response; highway routing). NRC certifies Type B and fissile package designs, approves package quality assurance programs for its licensees, provides technical support to DOT, and conducts inspections of licensees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Memorandum of Understanding (July 2, 1979) coordinates DOT and NRC duties; rulemaking developed in coordination with NRC to maintain consistent standards and publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal preemption of state/local/tribal requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: This rule preempts State, local and Indian tribe requirements on covered subjects (designation/classification of hazardous material; packing/repacking/handling/labeling/marking/placarding; shipping documents; reporting of unintentional release; design/manufacture/testing of packagings) unless they are 'substantively the same.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Federal hazardous material transportation law contains an express preemption provision (49 U.S.C. 5125(b)); the effective date of federal preemption must be published and be no earlier than 90 days and no later than two years after issuance (effective date for this rule's preemption is October 1, 2004).

rubrics_metrics.name: No small-business differing-compliance exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency determined it is not possible to establish exceptions or differing compliance standards for small businesses and still accomplish the objectives of Federal hazmat law for radioactive materials transportation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory Flexibility Act consideration led to accommodations such as extended transition periods rather than differing substantive standards; the rule includes an analysis of potential economic impacts on small entities.
